NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
Proposed intervention: a coordinated three-axis parameter/procedure change — (1) VFD dv/dt limit set to minimum (≤500 V/μs) and switching frequency reduced to 2 kHz; (2) gland sealing procedure revised to a two-stage torque sequence with a 1-hour settle using existing self-amalgamating tape; (3) well-level setpoints lowered so the cable termination is exposed to air during pump-off cycles, and a maximum continuous run time of 30 min enforced with a minimum 30 min off-time.  
Standard practice: VFD runs at default dv/dt (~2000 V/μs) and switching frequency (4–8 kHz); gland sealing uses a single-stage torque per manufacturer; well-level control uses fixed start/stop levels with no run-time limit.  
Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing practice is independent VFD parameter tuning (e.g., only reducing switching frequency for bearing current mitigation) or standalone gland re-torquing. The departure is the **simultaneous, interlocked scheduling** of all three axes: the VFD dv/dt reduction is paired with a duty-cycle that guarantees dry periods, and the gland procedure is timed to the same off-windows — a combined arrangement that attacks the water-tree driving physics (high dv/dt stress + continuous moisture) at every lever the constraints allow.  
Mechanism: reduces the electric-field stress at insulation defects by lowering dv/dt and impulse count, while the gland procedure and scheduled dry periods reduce moisture concentration at those defects.

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: water-tree growth rate ∝ (E)^n · f(dv/dt) · [H₂O] where E is local field at defects, f(dv/dt) captures partial-discharge inception sensitivity to voltage rise time, and [H₂O] is moisture concentration in the insulation.  
Magnitude verification: reducing dv/dt from 2000 to 500 V/μs lowers the PD inception voltage margin by ~40% (IEEE 1434 data for XLPE); cutting switching frequency from 6 kHz to 2 kHz reduces voltage impulses by 67%; a 30-min dry period every hour allows surface moisture to diffuse out, lowering [H₂O] at defects by an estimated 30–50% (diffusion time constant ~hours for XLPE). Combined effect: >70% reduction in tree-growth rate.  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = dv/dt (V/μs) and moisture content at insulation defects; the mechanism moves dv/dt **down** by 75% (2000→500 V/μs) via VFD parameter retuning, and moves moisture content **down** by periodic drying via well-level scheduling; this **reduces** the failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
| # | Component / Action | Generic Class / Stated Item | Attachment Point in Stated Infrastructure | Operating Parameter(s) & Values | Procurement Tag |
|---|-------------------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | VFD dv/dt limit parameter | Existing VFD (stated) | VFD control panel | Set dv/dt limit = 500 V/μs (or lowest available) | (c) |
| 2 | VFD switching frequency parameter | Existing VFD (stated) | VFD control panel | Set switching frequency = 2 kHz | (c) |
| 3 | Gland sealing procedure | Existing cable glands & self-amalgamating tape (standard practice bill) | Cable termination at well head & pump | Apply two layers of tape; torque to 50% spec, wait 1 hr, torque to 100% spec | (c) |
| 4 | Well-level stop setpoint | Existing level controller (stated) | Wet well level controller | Lower stop level 0.5 m below cable termination elevation | (c) |
| 5 | Pump duty-cycle limit | Existing pump controller / VFD (stated) | Pump control logic | Max continuous run = 30 min; min off-time = 30 min | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
Standard practice bill: VFD at default settings (no config cost), single-stage gland torque (standard labor), fixed level setpoints (no config cost), continuous run as demanded (no curtailment).  
Intervention bill rows 1–5: all are parameter/procedure changes on existing equipment — same procurement class (c) as standard practice’s own configuration steps.  
Installation/commissioning burden: VFD parameter changes take <15 min each via keypad; gland procedure adds 1 hr wait per termination (two terminations → 2 hr extra labor); level setpoint and duty-cycle changes take <10 min via controller. Total added labor ≤ 3 hr — same burden class as a routine maintenance visit.  
Operational loss: duty-cycle limit caps pump at 50% duty cycle. During sustained high-inflow events, peak throughput is reduced by up to 50% (explicit loss: 0.5 × pump rated flow × duration of high inflow). This loss is priced and counted against parity; it is the only operational cost.  
Conclusion: same-or-lower burden class (added labor is within a standard maintenance shift; operational loss is explicit and bounded).

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol:  
1. Select two identical submersible pump cables in the same wet well (same XLPE type, age, VFD model).  
2. Cable A (test): apply full intervention (rows 1–5). Cable B (control): keep standard practice settings.  
3. Instrumentation: temporary partial-discharge (PD) coupler at VFD output and at motor terminals (existing PD monitoring port if available; otherwise clamp-on HFCT for test duration only). Insulation resistance (IR) measured with 5 kV megger at monthly intervals.  
4. Duration: 90 days (covers multiple wet/dry cycles).  
5. Pass/fail thresholds:  
   - PD magnitude (peak-to-peak) at motor terminals: Cable A must show ≥30% reduction vs Cable B at day 90.  
   - IR trend: Cable A must not decrease >10% from baseline; Cable B may decrease.  
   - No phase-to-earth fault on either cable during test.  
Kill criterion: if Cable A suffers a phase-to-earth fault, or if PD magnitude on Cable A exceeds Cable B at any monthly check, the intervention is falsified.
